text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking we should move RBAC enforcement for console dashboard queries down into the query layer instead of doing it in the BFF. Reasons: single enforcement point, simpler frontends, and easier to verify with SQL policies. Thoughts?

kevin: Curious about perf hit. Every dashboard widget could fire many queries. If RBAC adds joins or filters at query time we might lose caching and increase p99s. :thinking:

olivia: Agreed on perf concerns. One option: keep a lightweight app-layer check for coarse access and push fine-grained row filtering into the DB via RLS/materialized views. That gives both safety and precompute opportunities.

maria: Example idea: apply tenant + role filtering as DB-level policies and expose only prefiltered materialized metrics for dashboards. If a user needs ad-hoc queries, route through a sandboxed service with stricter rate limits.

sanjay: Big tradeoff is invalidation + multi-tenant cache blowup. Materialized views are great for aggregated metrics, but time-series/filters could explode the MV count. We could generate MVs for common rollups and fall back to streaming queries for rare combos.

kevin: Also think about batching and KV cache reuse in the runtime. If each dashboard tile issues a parameterized query that includes role filters, we need a caching key strategy that doesn't leak data across roles. Could use (query_hash, role_hash) as cache key.

olivia: Another layer: a lightweight query DSL for the console that maps to a small set of safe SQL templates. Those templates are pre-approved for RLS. That reduces arbitrary ad-hoc SQL and simplifies analysis for perf.

maria: favorite concrete next steps: 1) prototype RLS policy for dashboards on staging, 2) create a small set of MV rollups for top 10 widgets, 3) add role_hash to runtime cache key. Anyone willing to pair on the prototype?

kevin: I can take the runtime cache + instrumentation side. Will add tracing/span tags for role_id and widget_id so we can measure p50/p95 changes.

olivia: I'll own the MV set and the DSL templates. I'll draft a short PR with example templates and a list of rollups.

maria: Sanjay — can you do the invalidation strategy doc? We need TTL heuristics and a plan for when to drop vs recompute.

sanjay: Yep. I'll sketch two modes: event-driven invalidation for near-real-time metrics, TTL for lower-cost ones. Will include simple formulas for cost vs freshness.

kevin: Quick note: if we push enforcement to DB, test harness should include a perf matrix: N widgets x M users x K roles to ensure we don't regress at 99th.

maria: Good call. We'll create a small benchmark harness in eng-infra that simulates console traffic patterns.

deploy-bot: deploy: branch/console-rbac-proto -> staging succeeded :white_check_mark:

olivia: Nice — will start running manual checks against staging MVs.

maria: Thanks team. Plan to sync next Tues 10am to review metrics and decide whether to canary to a subset of accounts.

kevin: Sounds good. I'll capture the instrumentation dashboard and share the link in the thread before the sync.

sanjay: Adding a reminder — consider fallback policy: if DB-level check fails under load, fallback to app-level deny (fail-safe). Document it in the RFC.

maria: Absolutely. Fail closed.

olivia: +1

maria: End.
